title: Schema-enforcement Series rebuilds must keep the input DataFrame index
answers: pyfunc predictions have extra rows or wrong values when input DataFrame was filtered or has a custom index and the signature has Array, Object or Map columns
model server returns misaligned rows for complex columns after enforcing signature
why does MLflow schema enforcement change my DataFrame index or add NaN rows
pd.Series rebuilt without index causes row misalignment in _enforce_named_col_schema
body:
Symptom: A model called with a DataFrame that has a non-default index (for example after filtering with iloc or loc) returns extra rows or places Array/Object/Map values in the wrong rows when the signature includes complex columns.
Root cause: mlflow/models/utils.py:_enforce_named_col_schema and _enforce_unnamed_col_schema rebuild complex columns as pd.Series from a list comprehension with no index, so they get a default RangeIndex. pd.DataFrame(new_pf_input) then aligns these Series to the scalar columns by label, which keeps the original index.
Fix pattern: Pass index=pf_input.index to every pd.Series that replaces a column in these functions, in both the named and unnamed branches, next to name=.
Constraints: Applies to any new branch in these two functions that rebuilds a column from a Python list. Scalar columns that are only cast keep the input index already. The rule is about the Series construction, not the caller.
applies: Applies to mlflow/models/utils.py column enforcement in pyfunc predict; any change that rebuilds a DataFrame column from a list must keep the input index.
says: Filtered input tables with nested lists return misaligned prediction rows or unexpected missing values.
Model serving produces extra rows when predicting on a sliced dataset with map fields.
Predictions scramble values across rows whenever the input table has a custom row index.
Ensure model inference keeps original row ordering when validating complex column types.
search: In pyfunc model column schema enforcement, rebuilding DataFrame columns from lists must preserve the input index. In mlflow/models/utils.py:_enforce_named_col_schema and _enforce_unnamed_col_schema, pass index=pf_input.index to every pd.Series replacing a column when enforcing signatures with Array, Object, or Map columns. This applies to any branch rebuilding columns from a list, while scalar columns that are only cast already retain the input index.
